issues.failure_explanation: The displayed definition characterizes functions of the form a(x)·b(t) with a single spatial factor and a single temporal factor. Such functions are not closed under addition (the sum of two separable functions is generally not separable), so the displayed set is not a vector space and cannot serve as the trial or test space for a Galerkin method. The intended object is the algebraic tensor product span{a(x)·b(t): a ∈ V_h, b ∈ P_p(I_n)}, i.e. finite sums of separable functions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the single-product characterization with the finite linear span of separable functions, i.e. define P_{p}(I_n;V_h) = P_{p}(I_n) ⊗ V_h = span{a(x)b(t): a ∈ V_h, b ∈ P_p(I_n)}. No downstream argument changes.
issues.overall_effect: As written the discrete trial and test spaces of methods (Walkington:method) and (Walkington:method-time-semi-discrete) are not vector spaces, so the methods and every a priori and a posteriori result built on them are ill-defined until the definition is corrected to the full tensor product.
issues.title: Tensor product space defined as set of rank-1 separable functions, not a vector space
issues.why_classification: The correction to the definition is immediate and local, and every proof and guarantee in the paper is written for the correct tensor product space, so all claims and rates survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The equivalent definition in display (equivalent-definition-Pcalpt) imposes three boundary conditions (two value conditions and one derivative condition) on a polynomial in P_{p_n^t}(I_n;X) which has p_n^t+1 degrees of freedom. For p_n^t = 2 the orthogonality condition is vacuous and the three boundary conditions give 3 = 2+1 equations for 3 unknowns, which is consistent with the original definition. For p_n^t = 1 the three boundary conditions give 3 equations for 2 unknowns and are generally inconsistent (they would require w(t_n) = w(t_{n-1}) + w'(t_n)·τ_n). The stated assumption only requires p_n^t ≥ 2 for n ≥ 2, so p_1^t = 1 is admissible and the equivalence claim fails on the first interval.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis p_n^t ≥ 2 for all n = 1,…,N (extending the existing assumption to include n = 1), or state that the equivalent definition is used only when p_n^t ≥ 2 and otherwise the original definition applies.
issues.overall_effect: For p_1^t = 1 the equivalent definition is inconsistent and the operator P_p^t is not defined by it on I_1. The proof of Lemma lem:added-1 and Proposition proposition:Pcaltildept-L2-approx reference the equivalent definition, although the original definition (which is well-defined for p = 1) suffices. The advertised parameter range p_1^t ≥ 1 is misleading.
issues.title: Claimed equivalence of two definitions of the operator P_p^t fails for polynomial degree p_n^t = 1
issues.why_classification: Adding the single local condition p_1^t ≥ 2 resolves the inconsistency without changing any rate or guarantee; alternatively the proofs can be rewritten using the original definition, which is well-defined for all p ≥ 1.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
All other~$\gimel_j$ terms, $j=1,2,4,5,6,8$,
already gave $\mathcal O(\tau^\p)$ rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary's second estimate (for s ≤ p) claims the rate τ^{s−1/2} for the combined L^∞(L^2)/H^1 error norm. The proof asserts that terms ℭ_j for j = 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8 'already gave O(τ^p) rates,' so only ℭ_3 and ℭ_7 need the L^∞ trick. However the bounds in Theorem theorem:h-p-convergence give ℭ_5^2 = O(τ^{2(s−1)}) and ℭ_6^2 = O(τ^{2(s−1)}) (using only s−1 derivatives of Δ_x u and of u″), yielding a rate of τ^{s−1} for the norm. Since s−1 < s−1/2 for all s, the overall rate established by the proof is τ^{s−1}, not τ^{s−1/2}. The claim that these terms give O(τ^p) is false whenever s ≤ p (since s−1 < p in that regime). The rate τ^{s−1/2} is achievable with the assumed regularity (u has s+1 time derivatives, so Δ_x u has s+1 time derivatives and the approximation rate improves to (τ/p)^{2(s+1)}), but the proof does not carry this out.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the bounds for ℭ_5 and ℭ_6 in Theorem theorem:h-p-convergence using the full assumed regularity (s+1 time derivatives of Δ_x u and s+1 spatial derivatives of u″ in place of s−1 in each case), which raises their rate to O(τ^{2(s+1)}) and leaves ℭ_1, ℭ_2, ℭ_8 as the bottleneck at τ^{s−1/2}, or weaken the second rate to τ^{s−1}.
issues.overall_effect: The second ('Sobolev-optimality') rate of Corollary corollary:h-p-convergence-alpha=1 is unsupported as written. The analysis yields τ^{s−1}, one order slower. The numerical claims in Section section:numerical-experiments citing this rate as 'optimal' for test case 2 are correspondingly not backed by the theory.
issues.title: Second convergence rate τ^{s−1/2} in the corollary is not established; analysis only yields τ^{s−1}
issues.why_classification: The claimed rate is attainable with the stated regularity but requires re-optimizing the estimates for two terms in a nontrivial though contained argument; alternatively a limited one-order weakening to τ^{s−1} preserves a recognizably comparable convergence result. No new global proof architecture is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: For t ∈ I_n with n < m the function v(t) = ∫_t^ξ (u−R_{p+1}u_τ)(s) ds involves integration over intervals beyond I_n (since ξ ∈ I_m with m > n). Hence ‖v‖_{L^∞(I_n)} is bounded by |ξ − t_{n-1}| · ‖v'‖_{L^∞(t_{n-1}, ξ)}, not by |ξ − t_{n-1}| · ‖v'‖_{L^∞(I_n)}. The stated inequality silently replaces the supremum of |v'| over (t_{n-1}, ξ) by its supremum over I_n, which can be strictly smaller when |v'| is larger on later intervals.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the intermediate inequality by ‖v‖_{L^∞(I_n)} ≤ |ξ − t_{n-1}| ‖v'‖_{L^∞(0,T)} (or |t_m − t_{n-1}| ‖v'‖_{L^∞(0,T)}) and drop the intermediate relaxation through ‖v'‖_{L^∞(I_n)}. The final bound is identical.
issues.overall_effect: The intermediate bound for T_5 in the case p_n^t = 2 is invalid. However the subsequent step already relaxes ‖v'‖_{L^∞(I_n)} to ‖v'‖_{L^∞(0,T)}, so the final reliability estimate (initial-reliability-estimate) and its downstream consequence (reliability:estimate) survive unchanged.
issues.title: False L^∞ bound on test function v on I_n in the a posteriori proof for p_n^t = 2
issues.why_classification: The false inequality is a local proof step whose replacement by the correct bound is immediate and leaves every intermediate and final estimate in the proposition unchanged.
